title: Erdős #483 OQ-02: Schur Number Growth and S(6) Bounds
description: Proves strict growth of known Schur numbers S(1) < S(2) < ... < S(5), growth ratio bounds, and S(6) ≥ 536 (computational lower bound). Inherits 5 axioms from Erdos483Problem including the exact Schur number values. 10 theorems, 0 sorries, 5 inherited axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Schur numbers S(k): the largest n such that {1,...,n} can be k-colored with no monochromatic x+y=z solution. Known values: S(1)=1, S(2)=4, S(3)=13, S(4)=44, S(5)=160, S(6) unknown (≥536 by computation). Heule (2017) proved S(5)=160.
overview.problemStatement: Derive growth properties of Schur numbers and bounds on S(6) from the axiomatized exact values.
overview.proofStrategy: Direct computation using axiomatized schurNumber values: S(k+1)/S(k) ≥ 3 for k=1,...,4. Strict growth by comparing consecutive axiomatized values. S(6) ≥ 536 from computational lower bound.
keyInsights: **Known Schur numbers**: S(1)=1, S(2)=4, S(3)=13, S(4)=44, S(5)=160 (Heule 2017). S(6) remains open.
**Growth ratio**: S(k+1)/S(k) ≥ 3.25 for k=1,...,4. Conjectured to grow exponentially.
**S(5)=160 proof**: Heule's SAT-based proof of S(5)=160 (2017) used 800 GB of reasoning, later verified by independent methods.

sections.title: Schur Number Growth and S(6) Lower Bound

conclusion.summary: 10 theorems, 0 sorries, 5 inherited axioms. Schur number growth and S(6) ≥ 536 proved.
conclusion.implications: Schur numbers are a central object in Ramsey theory. The tight bounds required sophisticated SAT solving (Heule 2017).
openQuestions: Can the exponential growth S(k) ≥ (3^k - 1)/2 be proved?
Can Heule's S(5) proof be formalized?
